project_name: Crown Heights West Rezoning & Text Amendment
evidence_summary: Crown Heights West combined contextual protections with growth and Inclusionary Housing corridors. It arose from a five-year CB/elected-official/community process; CB8 approved 35-0 and all 13 CPC speakers supported, but local groups and the BP pressed for stronger mandatory affordability, anti-displacement measures, and boundary changes. CPC acknowledged those concerns yet approved without adopting all requests.
coder_notes: Support with major requested changes is not substantial opposition; the process itself is procedural and the unadopted affordability demands are unresolved.

evidence_summary: Domino's modified text and special permits enabled a substantially redesigned, denser mixed-use waterfront redevelopment. CB1 and the BP conditionally supported, while ten CPC speakers opposed aspects of affordability, sustainability, labor, open space, services, and scale. CPC modified Inclusionary Housing terms and the declaration created childcare, phased open space, and a community review mechanism, but rejected or deferred several affordability, planting, and governance demands, including a councilmember's request.
coder_notes: Civic organizations mostly supported with substantial requests rather than opposing the entire project; unresolved objections remain despite major concessions.

evidence_summary: Three SoHo special permits enabled a new mixed residential-commercial building and ten-space garage. CB2 approved 32-4, the BP approved, and two CPC speakers supported with none opposed. A declaration secured the landmark preservation program.
coder_notes: No substantive local bargaining is reported; companion reports repeat one combined hearing.

evidence_summary: Bulk and garage permits facilitated an 18-story mixed-use building. CB5 approved 36-3, but the BP recommended disapproval unless electric charging, car-share, affordable-unit distribution, and green-roof conditions were met. The applicant responded in writing and accepted some measures; CPC approved while not fully adopting every BP condition. Six speakers supported and one opposed.
coder_notes: A formal BP disapprove-unless recommendation is substantial opposition even with limited hearing opposition.

evidence_summary: A small C1-5 overlay legalized an existing East Harlem loading dock. CB11 approved 37-0, the BP approved, and two speakers supported with none opposed.
coder_notes: Literal commercial permission increases, but practical direction is none because the action only legalizes an existing loading operation.

evidence_summary: C2-2 overlays along Williamsbridge Road expanded commercial permissions for the project sites. CB11 approved 28-0, the BP approved, and the applicant was the sole CPC speaker.
coder_notes: No opposition or responsive change appears.

evidence_summary: A NoHo permit allowed penthouse additions while modifying rooftop recreation rules. At CB2's request, the applicant sharply reduced the penthouses and preserved more roof recreation; CB2 then approved 32-0 and the BP approved. Two speakers supported and a declaration secured preservation.
coder_notes: The net project capacity is essentially unchanged because penthouse floor area was generated by interior removals; the local objection was resolved.

evidence_summary: A special permit allowed retail in an existing Mercer Street building. CB2 approved 35-0 while requesting modernized marketing, arts or artisan tenants, and ADA access. The applicant documented online marketing and promised efforts and occasional cultural uses, but CPC approved without guaranteeing all requests; one speaker supported.
coder_notes: Marketing and cultural-use efforts are procedural; the limited promises are concessions, but the CB conditions remain partly unresolved.

evidence_summary: A special permit converted offices to residential use and added a penthouse at 66 Allen Street. CB3 approved 41-0, the BP approved, one speaker supported, and a declaration secured landmark maintenance.
coder_notes: The pre-hearing revision has no reported connection to local pressure; preservation obligations are substantive.

evidence_summary: A special permit enabled a new five-story South Conduit Avenue self-storage facility. CB10 approved 37-0, the BP approved, and one resident supported while noting possible traffic effects.
coder_notes: A concern voiced by a supporter does not constitute substantial opposition or a local demand.

evidence_summary: A landmark-transfer special permit enabled a ten-story office building at 3 St. Marks Place. CB3 rejected it 33-0, the BP and local councilmember opposed, Village Preservation opposed, and CPC heard four supporters and eleven opponents. CPC directly rejected objections about scale, congestion, office use, and insufficient public benefit while approving with a landmark preservation declaration.
coder_notes: The declaration is a substantive preservation concession, but it predates and does not resolve the core local objections.

evidence_summary: The 307 Kent map/text amendments converted M3 land to mixed-use and higher-intensity manufacturing districts. CB1 approved 25-5 and the BP conditionally supported while seeking affordable industrial space, local hiring, sustainability, and consultation. The applicant made hiring and green-design commitments and accepted environmental mitigation, but declined a recorded below-market industrial-space commitment; three speakers supported and two opposed.
coder_notes: The limited opposition does not meet the substantial threshold; the BP's unaccepted industrial-space condition is a specific unresolved objection.

evidence_summary: The St. Joseph's R6A-to-R7D rezoning enabled 287 affordable and supportive homes and services. CB6 approved 22-0, the BP approved, and three CPC speakers supported with none opposed.
coder_notes: No bargaining or opposition is reported.

evidence_summary: The Sutter Avenue R5-to-R6A/C2-4 rezoning enabled a modest mixed-use project with permanently affordable units. CB5 held no hearing. The BP conditionally supported, pressing for deeper affordability, tenant-selection participation, local nonprofits, and sustainability; the applicant made a 100-percent-affordable commitment and outreach promises, but CPC rejected limiting MIH to Option 1.
coder_notes: No CB vote is reported. Several BP requests are procedural, while the MIH objection remains explicitly unresolved.

evidence_summary: A C2-3 overlay enabled a one-story commercial building on Strang Avenue. CB12 approved 26-0, the BP approved, and two CPC speakers supported. CEQR E-666 supplies environmental mitigation.
coder_notes: The environmental commitment is substantive but not attributed to local pressure.

evidence_summary: The Northern Boulevard R3X-to-R3-2/C2-3 action enabled a three-story commercial/community-facility building. CB11 rejected it 27-10, two civic associations opposed rezoning rather than BSA relief, and one of two CPC speakers opposed. The BP conditionally supported with hiring, outreach, sustainability, and site-design requests; CPC approved without expressly resolving the board's core objection.
coder_notes: Procedural BP commitments and CEQR mitigation count as responses/concessions, but the CPC narrative does not explicitly attribute its approval rationale to local objections.

evidence_summary: The Eagle Avenue R6-to-R7-2 rezoning, text action, and permit enabled 83 affordable/supportive homes and community space. CB3 approved 14-6 and the BP supported with construction communication, height, accessibility, and sustainability requests. The design and declaration supplied public access, open space, mitigation, and communication commitments; all three CPC speakers supported.
coder_notes: The reported conditions were substantially accommodated, so no specific unresolved objection is coded.

evidence_summary: Brooklyn Yards combined a map/text upzoning and numerous permits for 270 homes, commercial space, public areas, and rail-platform construction. CB11 and CB12 approved by aggregate votes of 65-4 and the BP conditionally supported. The applicant withdrew a workforce MIH option, altered parking, and accepted access, traffic, phasing, and rail coordination commitments, but CPC expressly rejected the BP's 40-space parking cap. Eight speakers supported and two opposed.
coder_notes: Formal institutions supported; two hearing opponents do not make opposition substantial. Counts aggregate the two boards once, not companion reports.

evidence_summary: The Steinway Street R5D-to-R6A/C2-4 rezoning enabled 22 homes, six income-restricted, and retail. CB1 approved 28-2 and one CPC speaker supported. The BP conditionally supported with M/WBE, local hiring, outreach, and sustainability goals; CPC approved without reporting a substantive project change or expressly resolving those conditions.
coder_notes: The BP conditions are procedural and remain unresolved in the CPC record.

evidence_summary: The 250 86th Street R3-2-to-R6B rezoning legalized existing buildings and a medical office without proposed enlargement, while MIH would govern future redevelopment. CB10 rejected it 36-0 over bulk, precedent, neighboring lots, and community-facility risks; one CPC speaker opposed. The BP conditionally supported outreach, and CPC explicitly rejected the CB's concerns while approving.
coder_notes: Literal zoning is an upzone, but current practical development direction is none because no enlargement is proposed and the report predicts no induced redevelopment.

evidence_summary: The Queens Boulevard R7-1-to-R8X/C2-4 rezoning enabled a 17-story mixed-use building with twice the existing-zoning housing and affordable units. CB6 approved 23-6 and the BP conditionally supported, seeking less parking, more affordability/supportive housing, local hiring, M/WBE participation, and sustainability. The applicant expressly declined the parking and supportive-housing changes in writing; one CPC speaker supported and none opposed.
coder_notes: The requests are meaningful but do not amount to substantial opposition because both institutions approved and there was no opposition testimony.
